ApiError.description: Body shared by every failed response.

catalogue.description: The catalogue saved from the App Manager; none when the one of the installation applies.

installed.description:
What the import installs or removes, so the NAS has these and no other. The system
applications and the ones the installation brings are never removed.

AppsConfig.description: The settings of the applications chosen at the export, each under its identifier.

Busy.description:
What is under way: the names of the operations of the applications, which a shutdown
interrupts, and the jobs of root, which hold it back.

Cache.description: One cache, with the application it belongs to.

CapabilityProvider.description: An application that answers for a capability, on a path the browser reaches.

Component.description:
A part of the NAS released on its own. The order is the order of installation: the wizard
first, which changes nothing that runs, then the gateway, then the launcher, which restarts.

ComponentUpdate.description: One component as the settings show it.

currentVersion.description: The version installed, when the component can say it.

availableVersion.description: A newer release, found by the last check.

Config.description: The configuration as the launcher exports and imports it.

launcher.description: The version of the launcher that exported it

desktop.description: Absent from a file of version 1: the desktop then stays as it is.

DesktopEntry.description: One shortcut of the desktop, in the order of the file.

DesktopIconSize.description: How big the icons of the desktop are drawn: `large` is the size they always had.

device.description: The disk or one of its partitions: the whole disk is ejected.

nasName.description: The name chosen in the wizard, which becomes the hostname; without it the default stays

themes.description: The theme of each type, for the type `theme` resolves to.

GeneralConfig.description: The general settings without the name of the NAS, which stays the one of the machine.

Health.description: Service state returned by the health check.

InstalledApp.description:
An application installed from a package. The version says what the NAS had: the import
installs the latest one.

Kind.description: A cache, made again when emptied, or a trash, whose content goes for good.

Level.description:
How much an upgrade matters, from the archive it comes from: `<release>-security`, the release
itself and its `-updates`, or anything else (backports, other sources).

LinkKind.description: How the NAS is connected to the network.

uuid.description: The UUID of the filesystem of the volume.

locked.description: True marks the disk as not removable.

MailStatus.description: What the account settings need to know of the mail application.

installed.description: The application that sends the mails is installed.

sender.description: It has an SMTP server and a sender: it can send a code to an address.

checkOnOpen.description: Looks for newer releases each time the App Manager is opened.

updateOnOpen.description: Installs what that check finds: it means nothing without the check.

NasUpdates.description: The components installed on the NAS and their updates.

NewTask.description: What an application sends to register an operation.

Order.description: The applications on the desktop in the order they are shown, first to last.

screenOffMinutes.description:
The minutes without a key or the mouse after which the monitor connected to the NAS goes
dark and into standby, from 1 to 240.

started.description: The start time accompanying the process identifier.

Removed.description: How many rows a clearing route deleted.

skipped.description: Files left out because they were found clean and did not change since.

planned.description: Files sent to ClamAV, when the scan knows it beforehand; 0 when it does not.

cacheFiles.description: The files the archive of the scans holds as clean, and the room it takes on the disk.

ResetBlock.description: Why the NAS cannot be reset here.

ResetState.description: Whether the NAS can be reset here, and why not when it cannot.

skipUnchanged.description:
A custom scan that leaves out the files found clean and unchanged since (the quick scan
always does): see `scan_cache`.

day.description: systemd day name, or * for every day. Time uses the NAS timezone.

Step.description: One step, as the page that waits for them lists it.

Task.description: One operation, as the widget lists it.

progress.description: Per cent, or absent when the owner cannot tell.

TaskUpdate.description:
What the owner sends while it works. Every field is optional: reporting only the progress is
the common case, and leaving a field out does not clear it.

progress.description: `Some(None)` (an explicit `null`) is how an owner says it no longer knows.

Themes.description:
The theme chosen for each type, by the id of its file in `src/styles/themes/`: the interface
draws the default for an id it does not know.

WifiProblem.description: Why no wireless network could be listed, for the page to say so instead of "none found".
